---
name: knowledge-discover
description: Understand or prepare an existing repository, resume an unfinished investigation, or investigate a knowledge gap during delivery. Publish supported product and engineering explanations with routes to code and tests. Use knowledge-maintain to update established knowledge after a known change.
---

# Knowledge Discover

Investigate the user's scope and publish what the evidence supports. Preparation also establishes where an agent should start and what work can be verified. This skill does not implement application changes or take ownership of the surrounding delivery workflow.

Read [publication rules](../../references/publication.md) before publishing. For preparation, read [repository integration](../../references/repository-integration.md). For unfinished work or resumption, read [continuity](../../references/continuity.md). Resolve resource links relative to this skill directory. Write generated documents in the repository being investigated.

## Start from the request

Identify the requested capability and intended outcome from the request and available task context. Read applicable instructions and the knowledge index, if present, then follow relevant documentation, implementation, and tests. Use repository search to fill gaps. Missing instructions or an index are starting conditions to handle, not prerequisites the user must supply.

State an inferred focus briefly when useful and proceed with independent investigation. Do not interview the user about routine filenames, search methods, or internal structures. Keep unrelated application work and documentation out of scope.

## Understand or prepare

Trace concrete behavior from its user-facing entry point through relevant implementation and tests. Inspect dependencies when they affect that behavior. Explain product purpose before implementation; do not infer product intent from code alone.

Reuse or correct a suitable existing page. Connect scattered material through navigation; create pages only for missing explanations. Publish supported findings during discovery—no separate Maintain invocation is needed. Group related findings and questions so the user can make necessary decisions together.

For preparation, add or update short host instructions and knowledge navigation. Find setup prerequisites and verification commands in repository evidence, run relevant available checks within scope, and record actual results and limits. An assessment may be complete while the environment still has a setup blocker; state the outcome requested and achieved. Missing dependencies do not themselves authorize installation or application fixes.

## Resume

Read the Markdown record and relevant published knowledge first. Check Git status, relevant diffs, and supporting sources, including uncommitted changes. Recheck affected conclusions, then continue the next unresolved action immediately. Do not recap or restart the whole investigation unless asked.

If no record exists, use available task context and evidence; ask only for context necessary to proceed. When conclusions are published and remaining work has a durable home, remove completed records and update incoming links according to the continuity rules.

## Investigate during delivery

Retain the original request and its existing issue or delivery document. Investigate the specific gap, distinguishing current implementation, confirmed requirements, and the proposed change. Do not replace the delivery task with repository-wide preparation or make application changes under this skill's authority.

Inspect available evidence before asking about intent. Present related decisions together with what is established, what remains unresolved, and what each choice changes. Continue independent work while answers are pending. Incorporate resolved answers into published explanations without a separate answer archive.

Save only necessary unfinished context when a question remains or the session is pausing. Link remaining implementation work to its existing owner; create a delivery note only if necessary to avoid losing the request.

## Finish

Review claims against inspected sources, check references, and preserve existing useful content. Report complete, partial, or blocked for the requested scope with document links, checks actually run, and specific remaining actions. Do not imply merged, deployed, tested, or ready without evidence.
# Publishing repository knowledge

Use existing documentation conventions. Keep each explanation in one authoritative place and link from other pages. Avoid empty sections, duplicate product descriptions, or a parallel knowledge system.

## Explain behavior and implementation

A small knowledge index can also serve as the product overview: explain what the product does, who uses it, a typical journey supported by evidence, and routes to capabilities. Do not invent users, rationale, or requirements when evidence is absent.

A capability page normally explains purpose, behavior, rules or examples needing elaboration, implementation flow, and relevant limits. Omit sections that add nothing. Create a shared engineering page only when it avoids repeating an explanation across capabilities.

Use a behavior table with these meanings; adapt labels to repository conventions:

| ID | Condition or trigger | Behavior | Code and tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stable identifier | When this applies | Actor/system action and observable result | Inspected paths and symbols; identify what each referenced test checks |

Preserve IDs when wording or row order changes. Never reuse an ID for unrelated behavior. Place references beside supported claims. Use links that resolve from the page and identify symbols or tests; line numbers alone can drift.

## Evidence and prose

| Source | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Inspected implementation | What examined code does under stated conditions |
| Existing test | What that test is written to check |
| Executed check | What passed, failed, or could not run in the recorded environment |
| Confirmed requirement | Intended behavior, with its source |
| Proposed change | Work considered or implemented, without claiming it already exists |

State conflicts rather than choosing intent without evidence. Name missing evidence or unavailable conditions precisely. Do not invent test results, reasons for behavior, completion, or deployment status.

Write concrete subjects, actions, conditions, and results. Define unfamiliar terms on first use. Explain why a referenced file or test matters. Add examples when rules or exceptions would otherwise be unclear. Avoid vague assurances and repetition.

Before publication, compare claims to inspected evidence, verify paths/symbols and links, check terminology, and ensure each paragraph adds information. Supported understanding belongs here; unresolved next actions belong in a minimal investigation record. Human answers become part of the explanation, not a separate default transcript or answer store.
# Investigation continuity

Published knowledge holds resolved understanding. One Markdown record per connected investigation holds only necessary unfinished context. Keep it in the investigated repository, following conventions or `docs/work/investigation/<question>.md`.

Save question and scope, relevant progress with links to published conclusions, open decisions and dependencies, next actions, and source context sufficient to recheck findings. Include relevant paths, revision information, and uncommitted changes; a commit ID alone cannot describe a dirty working tree. Link the original delivery request and other records needed to continue.

Update when an unresolved question or next action changes or the session is about to pause. Do not log every search/message, duplicate published explanations, create separate JSON/YAML saved state, or preserve human answers/transcripts by default. Temporary evidence maps and publication plans can stay in working context.

On resumption, read the record and relevant published pages, inspect current source changes, and recheck affected findings. Continue the next unresolved action without a routine recap or unrelated reinvestigation. Records must work in fresh Codex and Claude Code sessions without prior chat history or host-specific session IDs.

Remove a completed record only when useful conclusions are published, remaining implementation work is recorded or linked elsewhere, no unfinished task depends on information unique to the record, and incoming links have been updated. No separate archive is required by default. Preserve remaining questions in the connected record or an appropriate remaining record before removing the completed part.

# Repeated completion: pending message decision

Status: partial; paused for the user's answer next session. Scope is the repeated-completion question within the [confirmation-message delivery request](../../../delivery.md). Keep the original friendly-confirmation request and its implementation work there.

## Established progress

[Task completion behavior](../../task-completion.md) publishes the inspected implementation, existing test coverage, and passing six-test check. Repeated completion succeeds today and has explicit core test coverage. Preserve that success behavior for this message change unless the user explicitly requests a contract change. No evidence settles whether its friendly message should differ.

## Open decision

Should successful repeated completion use the same friendly confirmation as first completion, or a distinct message such as `Task 1 is already complete`? The example is proposed wording only.

- Same confirmation: keep a uniform success message; no need to distinguish prior completion state for wording.
- Distinct confirmation: still succeed, but communicate that no completion-state change was needed. Delivery must distinguish the prior state before `complete_task` sets `done=True`, or otherwise carry that distinction to the message logic; the current return value alone does not distinguish the two cases.

This is a product wording decision, not a missing dependency or failing check. The user requested a pause after necessary questions and will answer next session.

## Resume and remaining work

1. Read this record, the capability page, and delivery request. Check Git status and relevant diffs, then recheck affected evidence before using the user's answer.
2. Incorporate the decision into the capability page and delivery request as a confirmed requirement. Keep current behavior separate from pending implementation.
3. Leave application implementation and any needed core/CLI tests with `delivery.md`. This session authorizes documentation and existing local checks only, and prohibits application/test edits, commits, network services, subagents, and inspection outside this repository and installed skill resources.
4. Once the decision is published and remaining implementation work is captured in delivery, remove this record and update its incoming links in the capability page and delivery request.

## Source context

Investigated on 2026-10-01 at HEAD `f7d89cfa5f8fba386f4c948527e90fed04d2da18`. The working tree was clean at the start. Session changes are documentation only: navigation in `README.md`, progress in `delivery.md`, new `docs/task-completion.md`, and this record. `docs/export-notes.md` remains unchanged.

Relevant sources: [CLI `main`](../../../tasklist/cli.py), [core `complete_task`](../../../tasklist/tasks.py), and [tests](../../../tests/test_tasks.py), especially `test_complete_marks_done`, `test_repeat_completion_is_idempotent`, and `test_missing_id_rejected`. No CLI tests or approved repeat-specific wording were found in the repository.
# Task completion

The local task list lets a person mark a task complete by numeric ID. The [README](../README.md) describes the CLI and local JSON storage. The [delivery request](../delivery.md) calls for a friendly confirmation message; that message is not implemented.

## Current behavior

| ID | Condition or trigger | Behavior | Code and tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| COMPLETE-01 | Complete an existing unfinished task | Set `done` to `True` and return the task. | [tasks.py](../tasklist/tasks.py), `complete_task`; [test_tasks.py](../tests/test_tasks.py), `test_complete_marks_done` checks both the returned task and stored in-memory state. |
| COMPLETE-02 | Complete an existing task whose `done` is already `True` | Succeed and return the task with `done=True`. Completion is idempotent: repeating it leaves the completion state unchanged. | [tasks.py](../tasklist/tasks.py), `complete_task` has no rejection or separate branch for completed tasks; [test_tasks.py](../tests/test_tasks.py), `test_repeat_completion_is_idempotent` starts with a completed task and checks that the returned task is still done. |
| COMPLETE-03 | Complete an ID absent from the list | The core raises `KeyError`; the CLI reports the error and exits with status 2 before writing the file. | [tasks.py](../tasklist/tasks.py), `complete_task`; [cli.py](../tasklist/cli.py), `main`; [test_tasks.py](../tests/test_tasks.py), `test_missing_id_rejected` checks the core exception only. |
| COMPLETE-04 | A CLI completion call returns successfully | Write the task list to the JSON file and print the returned task as JSON, for both first and repeated completion. There is no friendly confirmation or special repeated-completion message. | [cli.py](../tasklist/cli.py), `main`, calls `complete_task`, writes for non-list commands, then prints `json.dumps(result)`. No existing test exercises CLI output or persistence. |

For a task with ID 1 and title `Read`, either successful completion path prints `{"id": 1, "title": "Read", "done": true}`. This follows from the inspected CLI; it was not verified by a CLI execution. Repeated completion still writes the file, even though the completion state is unchanged.

## Evidence and delivery boundary

The implementation and the explicitly named idempotency test support preserving successful repeated completion as the existing contract. Rejecting it would change that contract. Neither the test nor the delivery request establishes a requirement for distinct wording. A special message is therefore an unresolved proposal, not current behavior or an approved requirement. See the [open decision and resumption record](work/investigation/repeated-completion.md).

On 2026-10-01, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` passed all six existing tests. These tests exercise in-memory operations, including an already completed task; they do not establish CLI message behavior. No application code or tests were changed.
# Confirmation-message change

Add a friendly confirmation message when the user completes a task. Investigate repeated completion before implementing the message. Application implementation remains pending.

Investigation is partial: [current completion behavior and test evidence](docs/task-completion.md) support keeping repeated completion successful. Whether to give it a distinct friendly message remains a product decision; no wording has been approved. The [unfinished investigation](docs/work/investigation/repeated-completion.md) records the question and next steps for the next session. Implementation and any necessary test changes remain owned by this delivery request.
# Local task list

A command-line task list for one person, stored in a local JSON file. Add a task, list tasks, and complete a task by its numeric ID. Python 3.10 or later is required; there are no third-party dependencies.

Run from this directory:

```sh
python3 -m tasklist.cli --file /tmp/example-tasks.json add 'Review a document'
python3 -m tasklist.cli --file /tmp/example-tasks.json list
python3 -m tasklist.cli --file /tmp/example-tasks.json complete 1
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The core functions also work in memory. Persistence is provided by the CLI; this is not a web service or a multi-user database.

See [task completion behavior](docs/task-completion.md) for current completion rules and evidence, and the [confirmation-message delivery request](delivery.md) for pending work.
# Future export work

CSV export has not been implemented. Preserve this note while documenting task completion. The proposed column order is ID, title, done. No export feature or delivery date is promised.
